sectionProgressions.romanNumerals: I7 - IV7 - I7 - V7 - IV7 - I7
sectionProgressions.description: Driving 12-bar funk blues progression with tight rhythm guitar stabs and palm-muted fills
Harmonized guitar solo section where Joe Walsh (Les Paul) and Don Felder (Stratocaster) trade blistering leads

harmonicFunction: E7 (I7) - Heavy, swaggering dominant tonic that anchors the syncopated groove
A7 (IV7) - Funky subdominant expanding the blues-rock harmony with rich horn-like color
C7 (♭VI7) - Borrowed flat-sixth dominant chord providing a dramatic harmonic twist before the turnaround
B7 (V7) - Classic dominant chord delivering maximum tension before resolving back to E

techniques.name: Syncopated 16th-Note String Skipping & Riff Muting
techniques.description: Executing Joe Walsh's high-energy signature riff involving rapid 16th-note alternate picking, string skipping across the 6th, 5th, and 4th strings, and precise palm muting

notes: Riff starts with open low E string followed by quick double stops on the 7th fret of the A and D strings
Chromatic passing tones: Fret 6 to fret 7 on the A string providing the funky blues grease
Twin solo: 12th-position E minor pentatonic bends with biting treble attack
sequence: Lock into the 110 BPM groove with sixteenth-note alternate picking
Practice skipping between the 6th string bass root and 4th string blues accents
Incorporate fret-hand palm muting to achieve a crisp, percussive bite
Coordinate harmonized double-stops in third and sixth intervals during the solo breakdown
tips: Keep your picking hand wrist loose and close to the bridge for immediate palm muting
Accent the first note of each 16th-note group to establish the groove's natural bounce
Use a bridge humbucker with moderate overdrive for vintage 1970s bite without excess mud

techniques.name: Harmonized Twin-Lead Phrasing & Dorian/Mixolydian Bends
techniques.description: Trading blistering blues-rock leads and locking into tight dual-guitar harmonies in diatonic thirds and sixths, combining Joe Walsh's raw slide-like bends with Don Felder's precise melodic runs

notes: Dual harmonies: Thirds and sixths voiced across the G, B, and high E strings in 12th position
Bending nuances: Half-step and whole-step bends targeting chord tones of E7, A7, and B7
Tonal contrast: Walsh's thick Gibson humbucker tone complementing Felder's glassy Fender single-coil bite
sequence: Isolate the lead guitar phrases around the 12th-fret E minor pentatonic box
Practice the harmonized twin runs with a partner or looper pedal at moderate tempo
Emphasize the chromatic turnaround lick stepping up from C7 to B7
Lock into the final chord hit and sustain with natural amp feedback
tips: Match your vibrato speed and bend pitch exactly to your guitar partner for seamless harmony
Keep the right-hand pick angle slightly slanted for a snappy, biting funk-rock attack
Back off guitar tone slightly if your treble becomes overly piercing in the upper registers

sections.name: Iconic Opening 16th-Note Riff
sections.description: The immortal Joe Walsh guitar riff that defined the hard-rocking side of the Eagles' Hotel California album.
notes: Crisp alternate picking on the 16th-note string-skipping run
Light palm muting on the low E string
Pungent blues double-stop accents

sections.name: Verse Funk Groove & Palm-Muted Stabs
sections.description: Tight, syncopated rhythm guitar keeping the engine humming beneath Don Henley's vocals.
notes: Clean, percussive downstrokes on the low strings
Syncopated chord stabs locking with the hi-hat
Wide dynamic control under the verse melody

sections.name: Chorus Hook ('Life in the fast lane, surely make you lose your mind')
sections.technique: Open Power Chord Strumming & Vocal Cadence
sections.description: Explosive vocal hook propelled by driving open E, A, and B power chords and Walsh's ringing chord accents.
notes: Solid downstroke pick attack on chord changes
Let the open low E string ring with authority
Support multi-part vocal harmonies

sections.name: Verse 2 Syncopated Funk Interplay
sections.description: Don Felder and Joe Walsh lock together with complementary rhythm tracks, adding 9th chord extensions and snappy chicken-picking fills.
notes: Interlocking syncopated parts
Sharp offbeat stabs on beats 2 and 4
Clean tonal separation between two guitars

sections.name: Joe Walsh & Don Felder Twin-Lead Solo Duel
sections.description: One of rock's most famous guitar duels: Walsh's gritty, screaming Les Paul bends trading licks with Felder's laser-focused Stratocaster runs before harmonizing in soaring thirds.
notes: Singing full-step bends at the 14th and 15th frets
Tight, synchronised dual-guitar harmonization
Aggressive pick attack with valve overdrive sustain

sections.name: Outro Funk Jam & Final Decrescendo
sections.description: The band locks into an irresistible extended funk groove on the opening riff while Walsh and Felder trade screaming blues licks all the way to the final abrupt stop.
notes: Full band energy maintained to the end
Improvised blues pentatonic flourishes
Tight unison stop on the final E hit

beginner.title: Main Riff Mechanics & Tempo
steps: Learn the fret positions for the opening lick at 70 BPM
Focus on alternating down-up pick strokes across the string-skipping leap
Play the root-5 and root-6 dominant 7th chords (E7, A7, B7) in the verse

intermediate.title: Groove Locking & Chromatic Runs
steps: Build the opening riff up to the original 110 BPM tempo with crisp palm muting
Execute the chromatic approach notes cleanly on the A string
Lock into the funk pocket with tight rhythm section accents

advanced.title: Twin Guitar Lead Harmonies & Solo Phrasing
steps: Transcribe and perform Joe Walsh's aggressive pentatonic bends in the solo
Learn Don Felder's harmonized counter-melody and dual-guitar trading lines
Master the dynamic interplay between two lead guitars playing in tight harmony

10 minutes: Syncopated funk rhythm comping on E7 and A7 with crisp palm muting
